Reference / cell

cell#

A mutable value for synchronous code.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let total = Cell(0);
for items -> item { total.replace(total.value() + item.price()); }
total.value();

Description#

A mutable value for synchronous code.

Cell(value: initial) holds one value; value() reads it and replace(value) puts a new one. It is the mutable variable of synchronous code: an accumulator a loop updates, a position a parser advances, headers gathered while reading.

A Cell stays in synchronous code, and the compiler checks it: an async action cannot create, receive or use one. Object fields, enum payloads and once-let caches cannot hold one. A Cell cannot be hidden in any, a role or a generic parameter (Cell itself and builtin collections keep its type visible).

An action capturing a Cell or another frame-bound action, and a bound action on a Cell, stays in its synchronous frame. It may be called locally, bound to a local, or captured by another such action. It cannot be returned, passed to any action (including synchronous callbacks), stored, boxed or spawned. Functional-operation blocks run in the current frame and may use a Cell. With no suspension point in synchronous code, every read and write is whole with respect to tasks. State shared between tasks is async/atomic's Atomic.

A Cell is a value container, not a resource: it needs no close() and holds no OS resource. Values read from it are ordinary immutable Okkama values; cells compare by identity.
